description: Evidence-driven investigation for connection-reset-style bugs where the obvious explanation is probably wrong — a WebSocket dropping at a suspiciously exact interval, intermittent "connection reset by peer", a proxy/CDN symptom not matching the blamed layer, recurring DB pool-exhaustion despite pool-size bumps, or a scheduled job failing intermittently with no visible config difference. Use before committing to a root cause or fix — including "just restart it" or "just bump the pool" — without a concrete artifact behind it; when a teammate wants blanket retries over flakiness; when a fix for this bug class needs review before shipping; when an incident gets assumed "same as last time"; or when a green health check is trusted as proof the whole system is fine. Also trigger when someone is confident after a long session and wants to ship immediately. Not for writing new networking code, protocol explanations, or bugs already fully explained by a reproducible root cause.
